header.title: Open cross-task collaboration — attribution, audit, and denial copy
header.description: Agents may now write to any task they can read. These are the three surfaces that keep that legible: whose authority a comment rode, what an edit changed, and — when a write is refused — which boundary fired and what to do instead.

s1.title: “Fable · for Dotta” on a cross-task agent comment
s1.description: An agent commenting on a task it is not assigned to names the responsible user whose authority it rode. The assignee's own comments stay unchipped — that is the ordinary case, and chipping every bubble would be noise.
s1.frameUnknownUser: Responsible user not in the loaded directory
s1.frameLongName: Long user name truncates in the chip
s1.bodyOwn: Rebased onto master and re-ran the containment suite; all green.
s1.bodyCross: Dotta asked me to flag that the retry window here overlaps TASK-482. Worth a look before you close this.
s1.bodyFallback: Falls back to a generic label rather than printing a raw user id.
s1.bodyLong: The chip caps its width and truncates; the tooltip carries the full name.

s2.title: Every PATCH says who changed what, and under which authorization
s2.description: Required for agent and board edits alike. Before/after per field, the responsible user behind the write, and the authorization reason that let it through.
s2.verbStatus: changed the status from todo to in progress
s2.frameBoardEdit: Board (human) edit — audited the same way
s2.frameMulti: Reassignment, blockers, and work mode in one write
s2.frameOlder: Older activity row — no receipt, renders unchanged

s3.title: Every wall names the boundary, who can act, and the sanctioned path
s3.description: A real incident burned a full detour discovering a workaround behind an opaque 403. These are all the ways an issue write can now be refused — the same copy the API error body carries.
s3.frameBefore: Before — what the incident actually saw
s3.beforeNote: No boundary named, nobody named, no path forward. The workaround (create a child issue) had to be discovered by trial and error.

header.description: Replaces the current pattern where a Myrmidon-authored warning renders inside a user-style chat bubble. The notice is one container, system-styled, with hidden-by-default operational metadata. Tone is conveyed by icon, label, and color together so it stays accessible.

before.note: Author reads as <you>You</you> even though the author is the Myrmidon system. Two containers stack the warning inside a user-style bubble, and operational evidence is always visible.

design-guide.issueReferencePillNote: Used wherever a task is referenced — in markdown, the Related Work tab, and activity summaries. Pass <c>status</c> to show the target issue’s state at a glance. Use <c>variant="property"</c> for compact badges with direct navigation. Pass <c>onRemove</c> for a separate blocker removal control with reserved space. Use <c>strikethrough</c> for “removed” contexts.
design-guide.agentCapsuleNote: The brand “capsule is the agent” motif. A single agent reads as a tall pill that moves through three states as it comes to life. The online fill uses the live brand agent-gradient tokens (<c>--agent-Na</c> → <c>--agent-Nb</c>); <c>prefers-reduced-motion</c> skips the liquid rise and pulses and renders the final state.
design-guide.teamCatalogNote: Components from the Team Catalog browse/install surface (<c>/teams-catalog</c>). Fixtures are shared with the Storybook stories.
design-guide.teamRowNote: Installed teams collapse under <c>INSTALLED · N</c>; an out-of-date install (server <c>originHash</c> ≠ catalog <c>contentHash</c>) shows the amber <c>↑</c> badge (PAP-10256).
design-guide.teamCardNote: Square tile for the onboarding “Pick a starter team” grid. Selected tile gets <c>ring-2 ring-ring</c>. Drives the <c>useInstallTeamCatalogEntry</c> simplified flow.
design-guide.enforcementBannerNote: Persistent at the top of the Tools & Access surface. Tints to <c>denied-detected</c> when governed tool calls were denied or failed in the last hour. Observability only — enforcement lives in the tool gateway.

enforcementBanner.presentationalNote: Static governance copy with a tone. Used for the PAP-10400 trust-tier banner on Runtime and the effective-access banner on Agent → Tools. Pass <c>title</c>/<c>body</c> and an optional <c>icon</c>.

design-guide.actionCardNote: Signed payload sha256 + expiry surface on every variant (PAP-10400). The <c>stale</c> variant tints the border amber, banners the catalog-hash mismatch, strikes through the previous hash next to the current one, and renders <c>Approve</c> disabled until the request is re-issued.
design-guide.bindingsTableNote: Two-column key/value block with mono values. Lives inside <c>ActionCard</c> and is reused standalone in the audit row drilldown.
design-guide.toolAccessStatusNote: Policy decisions, connection/runtime health, and catalog quarantine all route through the canonical <c>StatusBadge</c> keys defined in <c>lib/status-colors</c>.
design-guide.composioNote: A broker connection (Composio) fronts many services, so its detail page lists toolkits with per-service state instead of one credential. Row state comes from Composio’s own account status, which is why there is a fourth <c>attention</c> state alongside the three the design asks for: an expired credential is neither connected nor still settling.
design-guide.envEditorNote: Reusable env-var editor (agents, projects, environments, routines). One shared grid, an in-field Text/Secret source switch, a fuzzy secret picker with a pinned “Create secret” item, automatic sensitive-value detection, and inline secret-health warnings. See the Storybook <m>Product/Environment Variables Editor</m> stories for all 10 states.
design-guide.resizablePanelsNote: Design-system wrapper over <m>react-resizable-panels</m> (Skill Studio D2). Drag a handle to resize; panels accept percentage or pixel (<m>minSize="240px"</m>) constraints and the middle panel is collapsible. Use anywhere a split view is needed.
design-guide.inlineBannerNote: Token-backed full-width notice (<m>brandBanner</m> tones). Use <m>info</m> for provenance/context and <m>warning</m> for paused/attention. Supports an optional bold title and a trailing actions slot. Replaces hand-rolled <m>bg-yellow-*</m>/<m>bg-blue-*</m> banners.
design-guide.builtInAgentBanner: Ships with Myrmidon and powers Briefs. It can be paused but not deleted.
design-guide.builtInGateNote: composes <m>PageSkeleton</m> + <m>EmptyState</m> + <m>InlineBanner</m> to render the loading / setup / pending-approval / paused / ready states of a feature that depends on a built-in agent.

design-guide.pageSubtitle: Every component, style, and pattern used across Myrmidon.
design-guide.collectionNote: CollectionToolbar owns shared geometry while each page owns its state and behavior. The canonical task row is opt-in during migration: status leads, unread work uses title emphasis, metadata remains stable, and the task identifier trails.
design-guide.dashboardRunsNote: The dashboard and Live runs page use the same compact cards. In-progress task icons animate across the app, including between runs, to represent task workflow status. Live indicators report active execution. Open a run to view its status and transcript.
design-guide.dialogSample: This is a sample dialog showing the standard layout with header, content, and footer.
design-guide.sidebarNavNote: Layout accepts sidebarSections to compose additional SidebarSection groups inside the shared sidebar. Use SidebarNavItem for each row, with sibling action buttons for starring or menus. The Chats section shows starred agents, the earliest-created agent when unstarred, then four recent agents without duplicates. Compose and star controls share a vertical column. Compose appears on hover or keyboard focus and remains visible on touch; starred icons remain visible. The picker searches all company agents by name or role without a subtitle, count, continuation labels, or footer. Task breadcrumbs support leading identity and trailing actions beside the label, including single-item task headers; see the Agent chat Storybook.
design-guide.outputEmptyNote: When an issue has produced no artifact work products, the Output section renders nothing at all (no placeholder card).
design-guide.actionCardMobileNote: Identical content; the three buttons stack full-width in the order Approve / Deny / Edit & re-sign, and the bindings table uses a 70px label column.
design-guide.provenanceNote: Shown wherever a brokered child connection appears, so the parent/child coupling is legible. Links to the broker's Services tab when the parent is known.
design-guide.repositoriesNote: Loading, errors, empty search, mobile, and short viewports are covered in the Project repos Storybook stories.
design-guide.recoveryNote: Recovery runs in the background. Task lists keep their ordinary status without execution badges. Active transcript headers keep saying Working during automatic recovery. Recovery decisions and attempts belong in the run log; there is no execution status card or reconciliation form.
design-guide.connectionIntentNote: The task card is the dialog host for the shared connection setup flow. Provider forms, validation, OAuth, access selection, and completion come from the same feature module as the full-page Apps setup; this card owns only audience, dialog, and task refresh behavior. Pending connections stay in the timeline beside a usable composer. The independently addressable Connections/In-task connections stories cover access, OAuth recovery, narrow layouts, completion, and historical outcomes.
design-guide.briefsPausedBody: Its built-in agent was paused 2 days ago, so new briefs aren't being generated.
design-guide.lifecycleChipNote: A derived lifecycle chip (amber) for attention states. The lifecycle chip is separate from the agent status vocabulary and only shows for <m>needs_setup</m> / <m>pending_approval</m>.
